title: Can a correct key look wrong to the decoder?
question: Across the pinned Round 19 skip and drift constructions, which decoders can recover known text when given the correct key?
reader_question: Could a decoder mistake the right key for a failed decryption?
summary: With the same planted message and correct key, the original beam can lose most runes while a permissive drift decoder recovers them. The repaired source control grid reproduces its gate decisions, with tiny score-rounding differences that fail the frozen bit-exact acceptance condition.
finding: For one paired-skip 240-rune control, exact recovery is 45.8% with the original beam and 100% with permissive drift. Across 20 gated groups per decoder, the original passes 0 and drift cost 8 passes 20. All 2,100 rows and 300 group decisions agree with source except tiny score roundoff in 88 row values and eight summary values; the original exact non-timing acceptance was not met.
limitations: Synthetic known-key English-derived text at 240/400 runes. Gate uses medians across seven seeds and does not establish every-seed recovery. No wrong-key calibration for all ten modes, unknown-key LP2 search or general cipher exclusion. The post-result 3e-15 score tolerance is diagnostic, not a retroactive change to the exact replay plan.
next_steps: Pair any proposed LP2 skip decoder with source-matched planted recovery tests and wrong-key controls before interpreting a failed or readable candidate search.
